summary: The Embassy of Equatorial Guinea in Washington says every visitor with a foreign passport must present a valid visa at the point of entry; visas are applied for at an embassy, and the UK FCDO also describes an online e-visa application. US citizens have needed a visa too since April 2023, when their exemption was cancelled.

payments.text: The UK FCDO says you can pay by credit card only at a few major hotels, including the Hilton and Sofitel; there are a limited number of ATMs in Malabo and Bata, some of which accept international cards, and local banks exchange cash euros, pounds and US dollars. Canada says the economy runs mainly on cash.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says crime ranges from petty theft and mugging to carjacking and armed robbery, with greater risk after dark in remote areas of towns, including around Malabo and Bata. It says police and military roadblocks are common, with regular reports of requests for bribes, that photographing government or military buildings or airports is illegal, and that you should always carry your passport or residence permit, or copies.

tips.text: US citizens no longer enter visa-free. Equatorial Guinea cancelled the exemption in April 2023, and the US Embassy in Malabo asks travellers to ignore websites that still say otherwise. It advises applying at least 60 days before you travel; the Embassy of Equatorial Guinea says a visa must be used within 60 days of issuance.
The UK FCDO says photographing government or military buildings or airports is illegal and you could be arrested and detained.

The UK FCDO says to carry your passport or residence permit (or copies) throughout the country: police and military roadblocks are common, and failing to show identification on request can lead to arrest and detention.

The UK FCDO describes an online e-visa application (72-hour processing; the printed e-visa letter is presented on arrival, where border officials issue the visa). Equatorial Guinea's own government publishes no eVisa page we could find.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Equatorial Guinea?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do. The Embassy of Equatorial Guinea in Washington states that every visitor with a foreign passport must present a valid visa at the point of entry; you can apply at an embassy, and the UK FCDO also describes an online e-visa application. That includes US citizens, whose visa-free arrangement was cancelled in April 2023. No official source we could read states the entry rule for citizens of the other CEMAC states (Cameroon, Chad, the Central African Republic, Congo and Gabon).

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Equatorial Guinea?
faq.answer: Yes. Equatorial Guinea cancelled visa-free travel for US passport holders on 24 April 2023, and its Embassy in Washington says every visitor with a foreign passport must present a valid visa. The US Embassy in Malabo advises applying at an Equatoguinean embassy at least 60 days before travel and ignoring websites that still describe the old exemption; the Embassy of Equatorial Guinea adds that a visa must be used within 60 days of issuance.

faq.question: Does Equatorial Guinea have an eVisa?
faq.answer: According to the UK FCDO, yes: complete the online visa application and upload the documents, allow 72 hours for processing, then print the e-visa letter and present it on arrival, where border officials issue the visa. Equatorial Guinea's own government publishes no eVisa page we could find.
